content: {"summary":"To capture a heap snapshot from orders‑api‑03 without triggering an OOM kill, pick a pod whose memory usage is well below its limit (≈ 60 % or less), then send SIGUSR2 to the process, wait for the snapshot file to finish writing, and copy it out before the pod exceeds its limit.","likely_cause":"Taking a heap snapshot when the pod is near its memory limit adds extra memory pressure that can OOM‑kill the container.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Writing a snapshot needs extra memory and can OOM‑kill a pod close to its limit","evidence_ids":["RB-004#3"],"quote":"Warning: writing a snapshot needs a lot of extra memory on top of the heap itself. A pod already close to its memory limit can be OOMKilled mid-snapshot"},{"text":"Select a pod whose memory is under about 60 % of its limit before snapshotting","evidence_ids":["RB-004#3"],"quote":"Snapshot a pod whose memory is still well below its limit (under about 60%)"},{"text":"Trigger the snapshot by sending SIGUSR2 to PID 1 in the pod","evidence_ids":["RB-004#3"],"quote":"`kubectl -n commerce exec <pod> -- kill -USR2 1`"},{"text":"After the snapshot file appears, copy it out of the pod","evidence_ids":["RB-004#4"],"quote":"`kubectl -n commerce cp <pod>:/app/<file>.heapsnapshot ./orders-heap.heapsnapshot`"}],"next_checks":["Verify current memory usage of orders‑api‑03 is below 60 % of its limit","Confirm the snapshot file appears in /app after sending SIGUSR2","Check that the pod remains healthy after the snapshot operation","If memory climbs too fast, consider a rollout with `--heapsnapshot-near-heap-limit=1` and a higher memory limit"]}
